hints.text: Fast running, vaulting, and dodging have separate controls. Practice them on safe ground before relying on them in a fight.
Advanced movement spends stamina. Leave yourself enough for the escape as well as the approach.
The Movement lesson shows your current bindings. Read it in Threads before trying an unfamiliar jump or dodge.
Put solid cover between yourself and a ranged attacker before approaching. An open field leaves fewer places to retreat.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Pick an escape route before entering a fight. Backing into another group of enemies can turn a retreat into a trap.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Keep distance from an imminent explosion and move behind solid cover when possible.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Keep explosive work away from supplies you cannot afford to replace. Leave yourself a clear exit before igniting anything.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Check the descent before stepping off a ledge. A staircase is easier to retrace than a blind drop.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Look at the landing before committing to a jump. Leave room to stop on the other side.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Feather Falling reduces fall damage. Check its enchantment description when preparing boots for climbing and exploration.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Water Breathing can buy time underwater. Check the remaining effect duration before swimming farther from air.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Plan your route back to air before diving. Turn back while you still have time to make the return trip.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Separate underwater scouting from a long work session. Prepare breathing protection before settling in to mine or build.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Fire Resistance helps against fire and lava damage. Check that the effect is active before approaching a hot crossing.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Build a secure route across lava before carrying out work nearby. Keep the return path visible.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Get clear of the burning area before returning to attack or collect items. Re-entering the hazard can undo your escape.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Leave room to escape when working under loose sand or gravel. Digging overhead can bring material down onto you.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Avoid crowding into a confined space with many entities. Leave room to move away from the group.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Check active status effects when damage continues after a fight. The attacker may be gone while an effect remains.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Wither can keep dealing damage after the hit. Reach a safe place before deciding whether to resume the fight.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Carry food you can eat before starting a long trip. Keep a reserve for the journey home.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Water at purity level 3 is safe to drink. Check purity before depending on a bottle for a long journey.
The water Curios slot can drink from stored water bottles as thirst drops. Fill it with safe water before leaving.
Rain Collectors need an open view of the sky. Keep the space above the collector clear.
A Rain Collector stores a limited supply. Bottle collected water so you have a reserve between showers.
Water Survival provides a Curios slot for empty bottles. Keep bottles available for refilling along the way.
Check the cold insulation on your clothing before heading into a cold area. Armor protection and insulation solve different problems.
Prepare heat insulation before traveling through hot areas. Check the clothing's temperature protection in its tooltip.
Body temperature and the temperature around you are different readings. Check both when choosing where to recover.
A prepared Cold Sweat waterskin helps change body temperature. Check its temperature before using it.
Plan stops in safer temperatures along a long route. Prepare clothing for the destination as well as the starting area.
A full hunger bar does not mean your nutrition groups are full. Check nutrition before choosing your next meal.
Choose foods that replenish your lowest nutrition groups. Repeating one meal may leave other groups behind.
Sugar makes nutrition drain faster. Check your food supply before relying on its short-lived benefits.
Check food tooltips before a trip. Frozen food needs to thaw before you can eat it.
Fall protection reduces risk, but a checked route is still useful. Inspect the way back before descending into an unfamiliar cave.
sources: minecraft@1.20.1: LivingEntity, Player, FoodData, DamageSources, MobEffects, EnchantmentHelper

hints.text: Threads Lessons are available from the start. You can read survival instructions before discovering the related card.
Press {threads} to open Threads during play. Return to Lessons whenever you need a reminder.
Loading lessons can also be read in Threads. A quick join does not mean you missed your only chance to read them.
Check the recipe in EMI before gathering materials. Better Content changes many familiar recipes.
Look up an item's uses as well as its recipe in EMI. A material you found may serve several different processes.
For a multi-step recipe, check the intermediate products before building the first machine.
A filled Rain Collector can be used with an empty hand to drink. Check the water's purity before relying on it.
Use a suitable empty container on a filled Rain Collector to take water with you.
Life choices last for your current life. Review the resulting properties before applying points.
Death clears your Life allocations. Review the stats screen as you prepare for the next journey.
A Hand Crank can power a small Create setup manually. Start with the machine you need, then connect its rotation.
Materials from several Font destinations can start seared metallurgy. Check the grout routes in EMI before choosing an expedition.
Andesite Alloy has casting and alloying routes in this pack. Compare the processes in EMI before choosing your setup.
Sequenced assembly recipes need their steps in order. Check the number of repetitions before setting up the line.
Follow the intermediate item through sequenced assembly. One pass through a machine may be only part of the recipe.
Tinkers tools can be repaired after use. Check the repair options before replacing a worn tool.
Repair your working tools before a long expedition. Check the station result before taking the repaired item.
Surface ore signs point toward underground deposits. Read the deposit family before choosing where to dig.
An ore deposit can appear in different host stones. Follow the deposit identity rather than expecting one background rock.
Keep small ore chunks from prospecting. Matching small chunks can be combined into a full chunk.
Look up your ore family in EMI before processing it. Different families follow different separation routes.
Check which concentrate a process produces before building around it. One deposit can contain more than one useful material.
Before using a Dimensional Font, read how its journey returns you. Prepare supplies before starting the trip.
Use a Font expedition to scout as well as gather. Note useful resources so a later visit has a clear purpose.
The vanilla End route is disabled in Better Content. Look for Dimensional Fonts to explore the available realms.
A heat network needs a way to lose excess heat. Check its surroundings and cooling before adding more heat sources.
Heat pipes exchange heat with their neighbors. Trace the connected route when a section stays hotter than expected.
Check the pressure required by a Pressure Chamber recipe. Having the ingredients alone is not enough.
Pressure Chamber recipes can require several items at once. Check the amounts before starting the process.
Ars Nouveau spells apply glyphs in order. Check the sequence when a spell behaves differently from what you intended.
Test a new spell on a suitable target in a safe place. Some effects need particular targets or conditions to work.
Relics gain experience through use. Read an item's abilities and use it where those abilities apply.
Check a relic's activation conditions before relying on it. Carrying the item may not be enough to trigger its ability.
Check which season a crop is fertile in before planting a large field.
Store surplus harvests while your crops are productive. A change of season can change what grows well.
Chunk anchors need their own resource supply. Check that supply before relying on distant machinery to keep running.
A working chunk anchor keeps a centered three-by-three chunk area ticking. Plan the machines you want to keep active around it.
A published schematic preserves a build's design, not its materials. Plan to gather blocks when rebuilding it.
Publish a design to the schematic library if you want to preserve it across world resets.
AE2 autocrafting uses encoded patterns. Teach the network a recipe before asking it to craft the result.
A stored pattern is the start of an autocrafting setup. Check the crafting request for missing inputs before confirming it.
Roads connect settlements through the wilderness. Following one can help you find another place to visit.
Pillager assaults are announced in advance. Use the warning to gather allies and prepare the approaches to your shelter.
Village markets accept matching trading-spirit colors. Check the merchant's trade before collecting a particular color.
The sky is not the final destination. Creating Space has rockets that can reach Earth orbit.
A future rocket will need more than a launch button. Its controls let you check destination, thrust, and delta-v.
A World Condenser can begin a successor world. Its interface explains the permanent reset before you commit.
A workshop can leave more than memories behind. Published schematics preserve its design for a successor world.
An AE2 network can learn recipes through encoded patterns. A future workshop could make familiar supplies on request.
Magic can keep a distant workshop running. Chunk anchors turn a continuing resource supply into active chunks.
Dimensional Fonts can take you beyond the Overworld. Each destination is another reason to prepare an expedition.
Ratlantis is an available Font destination. Its ruins and machinery await a better-prepared expedition.
The Bumblezone has resources and plants of its own. A future Font trip can be more than a hunt for familiar ores.
A familiar ore family can lead to several useful concentrates. More advanced processing opens reasons to revisit old deposits.
A relic's first use need not be its last surprise. Check how its abilities develop as it gains experience.
A spell is something you can write. Ars Nouveau glyphs let you combine a method of casting with a sequence of effects.
Fight where you have room to move. A narrow doorway can become a trap if enemies reach you from both sides.
When several enemies approach, retreat far enough to see the whole group before committing to another attack.
Check around a corner before chasing an enemy through it. The next room may contain another group.
Keep emergency supplies within easy reach. Searching a full inventory during a fight costs time you may need to escape.
Locate the ranged attacker before rushing forward. The nearest visible enemy may not be the source of the shots.
Use cover while eating or preparing an item. Staying still in a ranged enemy's sight gives it another clear shot.
Work back from the edge when arranging your inventory. Check your footing before returning to building or mining.
Leave a usable way back up when descending. The return climb may be harder with enemies nearby.
Night Vision improves visibility, not breathing. Prepare air or a breathing effect separately before diving.
Water Breathing has a time limit. Include the swim back to safety when planning how long to stay submerged.
Milk clears potion effects, including helpful ones. Check what you would lose before drinking it during an expedition.
Protection with a duration can end while you are still in danger. Check the timer before starting another task.
An empty water slot cannot replenish thirst. Check your equipped bottles as well as the supplies in your backpack.
Automatic drinking still uses the water you supplied. Check bottle purity before placing it in the water slot.
A Rain Collector can fill up. Move stored water into containers if you want room for the next rainfall.
A roof over a Rain Collector blocks collection. Give it open sky even if the rest of your water station is sheltered.
Compare food-group information before choosing provisions. Two filling meals can contribute to different nutrition groups.
Nutrition changes over time. Recheck the screen during a long trip, especially after relying on one type of food.
Sugar's benefits draw on your existing nutritional state. Replenish food groups instead of treating more sugar as recovery.
Pack foods that cover different nutrition groups. A stack of one food is convenient, but it may leave several groups low.
Food tooltips show thermal and spoilage state. Check stored provisions before choosing what to take on a trip.
Keep an edible backup meal when traveling in cold conditions. A frozen main supply cannot help until it thaws.
Merging food stacks combines their thermal state. Recheck the resulting stack instead of assuming it stayed unchanged.
Check the food tooltip after warming a frozen meal. Wait until it is actually thawed before relying on it.
Prepare a shelter route while the weather is still manageable. Waiting for a storm to arrive leaves less time to react.
Take changing weather into account on the return journey. A clear outward trip does not guarantee a clear trip home.
Avoid choosing an exposed worksite as your only shelter. Keep a safer place available when the weather worsens.
Stay aware of the storm while sheltered. Check conditions before resuming a long trip through exposed terrain.
When an assault is announced, check the approaches to your base. Choose where defenders can stand and where they can retreat.
Use an assault warning to repair equipment and gather food. Do those jobs before enemies reach the base.
An assault warning is time to regroup. Make sure allies know where the group intends to defend or withdraw.
Prepare a retreat route before an assault. A fortified entrance is more useful when you can leave if it is overwhelmed.
Some ChemLib gases can escape from stored items into the atmosphere. Check containment before stockpiling them near living areas.
A carried gas supply can be a source of pollution. Inspect the material before treating it as ordinary inventory cargo.
Natural hosted radioactive ore can behave differently after mining. Plan handling before collecting uranium or thorium forms.
Placing mined radioactive material back down does not necessarily make it inert again. Check its handling requirements.
Rail Beetles survey new routes at railway ends. A Beetle in the middle of a railway remains in driving mode.
Load rails, support blocks, and fuel before asking a Rail Beetle to build. Its prompt identifies missing supplies.
A Rail Beetle plans through loaded terrain. Explore the area before expecting a route farther into the cave.
Rail Beetles do not tunnel through solid rock. Clear a passage before planning a railway through it.
Rail Beetles do not plan underwater routes. Prepare a dry route if you want the machine to extend the railway.
Stop a Rail Beetle and apply its brakes before servicing engines or modules.
A Rail Beetle can burn cargo fuel when its installed engine is empty. Keep that in mind when choosing what to carry.
Rail Beetles prefer non-burnable support blocks. Supplying stone helps keep useful fuel out of the supports.
A Rail Beetle cannot install duplicate module families. Choose different upgrades for its available bays.
Long-range Beetle dispatch reaches already-loaded machines. It does not keep distant chunks loaded by itself.
Powered train fuel use rises with speed. Slowing a long journey can reduce its fuel cost.
A very fast train can consume fuel much faster than one near its normal top speed. Budget fuel for the speed you intend to use.
Estimate train fuel for both directions of a route. Increasing speed changes the fuel budget as well as the journey time.
Shafts, cogs, gearboxes, and belts contribute transmission stress. Account for the route as well as the powered machines.
A long rotational-power route has a cost. Consider placing the power source closer to the machines it serves.
Belt transmission loss considers the span between pulleys. Check long belts when reviewing a network's stress use.
Players can leave notes through Player Traces. Read nearby notes for information left by earlier visitors.
Traces are tied to their supporting blocks. Changing the ground can remove the traces attached to it.
Trace notes are written by players. Treat their advice as another player's observation rather than a guaranteed pack instruction.
A Trace note can include a recorded gesture. Inspect the marker as well as its text when reviewing a place.
The Bumblezone is a source of cultivatable food plants. Look for propagation materials when preparing a farming expedition.
Bumblezone cultivars support farming back in the Overworld. Bring propagation materials home rather than only a meal.
Breaking a Living Pollen Nursery yields seeds. Collect them when you find a nursery in the Bumblezone.
Collect more than one useful cultivar when exploring the Bumblezone. Different plants give you more options for future meals.
Ratlantis supplies components for scalable logistics. Check which component your next transport setup requires.
Plan a Ratlantis expedition around the logistics parts you need. Review the recipes before filling your inventory with loot.
A rat that replants needs suitable planting inputs. Check the supplies provided to an automated farm.
Check which input replants the crop or tree you are automating. An edible harvest is not always the correct planting item.
Ore processing can yield coproducts as well as the main metal. Leave storage space for the whole output.
Compare processing routes for the material you actually need. The highest primary-metal yield is not the only useful result.
Combine small chunks from the same deposit family. Mixing unrelated samples does not make a matching full chunk.
Keep ore stages distinguishable in storage. A chunk, crushed ore, and a concentrate belong to different processing steps.
A redstone signal disables a chunk anchor. Check nearby controls if an adequately supplied anchor stops keeping chunks active.
Different chunk anchors accept different resources. Match the supply to the anchor variant you built.
An anchor can run out of its resource. Include replenishment in the design of an unattended workshop.
Chemical storage has consequences beyond inventory space. Check whether the material can escape or emit radiation.
Escaped ChemLib gas enters the pollution system. Plan atmospheric handling alongside the process that produces it.
Different radioactive forms can have different emissions. Do not assume an ore, concentrate, and finished material behave alike.
The Life screen shows resulting properties. Review the concrete changes before committing an allocation.
Choose Life improvements for the activities you plan to do. Check their resulting properties rather than relying on the aspect name.
A new life is a chance to reconsider stat choices. Review your needs before repeating the previous allocation.
Check a recipe's output count when budgeting materials. Some pack recipes produce several components in a batch.
Check the process type shown by EMI. Ingredients for one machine may not work in a similar-looking machine.
Review alternate recipes before starting a large build. A route using materials you already have may suit the job better.
Route Beacons can guide a Rail Beetle toward a chosen destination. A railway need not grow only along its default suggestions.
Rail Beetles have optional drives for several power systems. A future railway can put more than furnace fuel to work.
A Bumblezone expedition can change what grows at home. Its cultivars offer more reasons to return than immediate food.
Living Pollen Nurseries hold seeds for future gardens. Exploring the Bumblezone can expand what you can plant at home.
Ratlantis can supply a future transport network. Check its logistics components when carrying everything by hand becomes limiting.
Rat logistics can extend into replanting crops and trees. A later farm can supply more than its owner can tend by hand.
Chemistry can affect the world around a workshop. Gases and radioactive forms give advanced storage its own engineering problems.
Some radioactive forms also emit heat. Advanced material handling can involve temperature as well as radiation.
A faster railway needs a different fuel budget. Planning speed becomes part of planning the transport network.
Maximum speed is not always the cheapest way to move supplies. A future railway can trade travel time for fuel savings.
The path to space includes an engineering table, an electrolyzer, and an air liquefier. Today's workshop can grow toward them.
Aerospace equipment brings advanced alloys into the workshop. Check those recipes when planning your next processing expansion.
You are at Death’s Door and healing is still locked. Move to safety; the next accepted hit can kill. Open Body to inspect the healing lock and your injuries.
Healing is available at Death’s Door. Restore HP to regain its protective buffer. Your injuries remain until treated; inspect them in Body.
You have matching injury medicine. Open Body, select the injury, and finish treatment in safety. HP healing leaves injuries.
Trauma amplifies existing impairments, not injury death odds. Avoid hits while stacks expire; treat injuries in Body.
Open Body to find medicine for untreated injuries. Injury type selects the cure; region determines the impairment.
Positive HP protects you from the death roll on the hit that empties it. At Death’s Door, further hits can kill. Healing restores HP; treatment removes injuries.
Body shows injuries and medicines. Complete treatment: one medicine cures one injury. Totems do not prevent player death.
Your sugar boost has become a crash. Check nutrition and recover somewhere safe; adding more sugar can extend the cycle.
Alcohol is currently impairing your control. Allow it to clear before attempting risky movement or fighting.
At least one nutrition group is below its supported threshold. Open nutrition and choose foods that replenish your lowest groups.
The food you are holding is frozen. Thaw it before eating; its stored temperature matters even after you carry it elsewhere.
A campaign is approaching you. Prepare cover, supplies, and an escape route before its attackers arrive.
Your HP buffer is low. Find cover and restore health before taking another hit. Inspect persistent injuries separately in Body.
Campaign attackers have arrived for you. Use cover and an escape route, and manage your supplies through the assault.
You survived your campaign. Check injuries, replace spent supplies, and repair defenses before the next journey.
